Kimberly — thanks for the fast turnaround and the attachments. We circulated the DPA to Legal and Procurement and they provided a short set of redlines (attached). Key questions from our counsel: 

1) Subprocessors: can you confirm whether any subprocessors have access to unredacted production data and whether any are located in India or Russia? Please flag any subprocessors that perform storage vs. pure orchestration/monitoring.
2) Transfer mechanism: procurement asks whether Redwood has a standing SCC execution path or if you require a DTA addendum per-customer. If the latter, we need the language and timing to sign.
3) Liability caps and indemnity: our GC requests a brief note on how Redwood typically handles cap/indemnity language for enterprise customers.

We prefer DocuSign. Procurement has requested the DocuSign envelope be initiated so they can attach the SOW and route for signature. Could you send the envelope link to me and cc procurement?

Attached: DataWave_DPA_redlines_2025-07-12.pdf

We’re aiming to finalize the DPA no later than Friday, July 18, due to the procurement gating. Appreciate any clarifying notes you can provide on the three items above.

Elena
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Sun, 13 Jul 2025 17:24:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA request + subprocessors / cross-border transfer question

Elena — thanks for the redlines and the timeline. I’ll address each point below and propose the immediate execution path.

1) Subprocessors: attached is a current export (redwood_subprocessors_2025-07-10.csv). Summary: no subprocessors located in Russia. We do engage a small set of subprocessors with personnel in India for monitoring and infra automation (listed as: AetherOps — monitoring, India; CacheFlow — caching & CDN, US/EU; VectorStore Inc. — managed index storage, US). None of the listed subprocessors have access to customer plaintext training data unless explicitly enabled by the customer (we default to pseudonymized telemetry for infra ops). I’ve annotated the CSV with purpose and access level.

2) Transfer mechanism: Redwood has a standard DPA plus an optional Data Transfer Addendum we attach for customers requiring explicit SCC language. For EU/UK controllers we append the SCC addendum and execute together with the DPA. We can provide the addendum today; the SCC mechanism is implemented as part of our standard privacy onboarding, not a separate long-running legal negotiation in our experience.

3) Liability/Indemnity: for Enterprise we are typically flexible — our standard DPA includes a mutual cap tied to 12 months of fees and limited indemnities; for strategic deals we can discuss tailored caps with Finance approval. If your GC has a target cap, please share and we’ll loop Finance.

DocuSign route: I’ve started a DocuSign envelope and uploaded Redwood_DPA_v1.0.docx (clean copy) so procurement can attach the SOW. Link below — please share with procurement and let us know when the envelope is routed so we can watch for signature events.

DocuSign envelope: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/ABC123def456

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v1.0.docx; redwood_subprocessors_2025-07-10.csv

Next suggested step: Elena, if procurement can attach the SOW and the DataWave redlines to the DocuSign envelope, Laura will review the submitted redline and propose any responsive edits within 24 hours. If that timeline works, we should be able to complete signature by July 18.
